frac_nl_equiv.teaches: equivalent fractions shown on stacked number lines
frac_nl_equiv.representation: two stacked 0-1 number lines of equal length in one boxed cell (thirds above, sixths below), the shared point boxed with a dashed vertical; write the equivalent fraction in the slot
frac_nl_equiv.why: No skill shows equivalent fractions as the same point on stacked number lines.

frac_wp_unlike.option: denominators "unlike" and task "is the answer reasonable?" (benchmark estimate)
frac_wp_unlike.name: Fraction Word Problems With Unlike Denominators (option)
frac_wp_unlike.teaches: adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators in context, and checking with benchmarks (2/5 + 1/2 cannot be 3/7)
frac_wp_unlike.representation: word-work cell: a story with unlike denominators, a fraction slot (numerator / denominator boxes) and a tick box reasonable / not reasonable
frac_wp_unlike.why: Fraction stories with unlike denominators and a reasonableness check close the 5.NF.A.2 half of the step.

function_machine.option: ftRules "+ then x", "- then x", "+ then /", "- then /" plus a "does the order matter?" pair
function_machine.name: Function Machines (two-step order)
function_machine.teaches: 2-step function machines with + or - first; the same two operations in both orders give different outputs; work backwards by undoing in reverse order
function_machine.representation: the kit function-table cell: In -> [+ 3] -> [x 2] -> Out machine boxes above a 4-row In/Out table; one or two blanks per row; order pair shows two machines with swapped boxes and asks for both outputs
function_machine.why: Existing function_machine proposal, scoped to what the rebuilt function tables still lack: + or - as the first step.

known_facts.name: Reason from Known Facts
known_facts.teaches: deriving new facts from a known one (24 × 15 = 360 so 24 × 16 = 384, 2.4 × 15 = 36)
known_facts.representation: a given fact and a list of related calculations to answer without recalculating
known_facts.why: No skill derives a new fact from a given one.

line_graph.name: Line Graphs
line_graph.teaches: reading and drawing line graphs that show change over time
line_graph.representation: a line graph on a grid with labelled axes; read values, find differences, or plot the points
line_graph.why: No live line graph skill; coordinate_graph plots points but never reads a joined line of data.

long_div_rem.name: Long Division with Remainders (option)
long_div_rem.teaches: long division by a 2-digit number with remainders written as r, a fraction or a decimal
long_div_rem.representation: a remainder-form option on long_div_2digit: the long-division bracket grid with a final answer slot in the chosen form (r, fraction or decimal), named in the instruction

long_mult.name: Long Multiplication and Division (4-digit)
long_mult.teaches: long multiplication of a 4-digit by a 2-digit number, short division of a 4-digit number, and choosing an efficient division method
long_mult.representation: a column grid with carry boxes and the placeholder row; option: short division bus stop with exchange boxes
long_mult.why: The longest written multiplication is 3-digit x 2-digit; 4-digit x 2-digit long multiplication and 4-digit short division are missing.

mean_missing.name: Find a Missing Value From the Mean (option)
mean_missing.teaches: using the mean x number of items = total to find a missing value, and the mean in a context
mean_missing.representation: a boxed list of numbers with one blank box and "mean = 6"; write the total, then the missing number
mean_missing.why: mean only asks for the mean of a list; the WRM step also finds a missing value from a given mean.

mental_add_sub.name: Mental Addition and Subtraction
mental_add_sub.teaches: mental strategies for large numbers: partitioning, counting on, compensating, near multiples
mental_add_sub.representation: a strategy prompt (round and adjust) beside each calculation
mental_add_sub.why: Y5 Mental strategies (prior learning wk W10 of Y6.B2.S16) has no skill.

mental_estimate.name: Mental Calculation and Estimation
mental_estimate.teaches: choosing and using a mental method for a calculation in any of the four operations (round and adjust, partition, double and halve, use a known fact), then checking with an estimate
mental_estimate.representation: one boxed cell: a calculation (4,999 + 2,350; 25 x 16; 3,600 ÷ 9); a bank of three method labels (round and adjust / partition / double and halve) with check boxes, tick the one that fits, then one answer slot; the method bank is a hint that fades on later pages, the answer slot stays
mental_estimate.why: The estimate skills already check a given answer ("Is the answer reasonable?"); no skill asks the pupil to choose or use a mental method.

metric_calc.name: Calculate with Metric Measures
metric_calc.teaches: calculating with metric measures in context, converting first when the units differ
metric_calc.representation: word-work cell: a story with two metric units, a conversion slot (1.2 kg = □ g) then the answer slot with its unit label
metric_calc.why: no skill adds, subtracts or compares two measures given in different metric units

metric_decimal_convert.name: Convert Metric Measures With Decimals (option)
metric_decimal_convert.teaches: converting metric length and mass in both directions when the amount or the answer is a decimal (3.4 km = 3,400 m; 650 g = 0.65 kg)
metric_decimal_convert.representation: a boxed cell: "3.4 km = [ ] m" with the unit fact (1 km = 1,000 m) above; support: a place-value shift chart as on place_value_10x, fading to the equation only
metric_decimal_convert.why: Length and mass conversions with decimal amounts (3.4 km = □ m, 650 g = □ kg) are dealt by no skill; capacity already deals 0.25 L ↔ 250 mL.
metric_decimal_convert.option: amounts "with decimals" and direction "to the larger unit" (units Metric)

metric_imperial.name: Metric and Imperial Units
metric_imperial.teaches: approximate conversions between metric and imperial units (1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb); imperial units including stone (1 stone = 14 lb)
metric_imperial.representation: one boxed cell: a conversion fact box (1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm) above one question; write the converted amount in the slot; the fact box fades on later pages
metric_imperial.why: imperial ↔ metric approximations (and stone) are dealt by no skill

miles_km.name: Miles and Kilometres
miles_km.teaches: converting between miles and kilometres using 5 miles ≈ 8 km
miles_km.representation: one B&W double number line in a boxed cell (miles above, km below, ticks paired 5 : 8, 10 : 16 ...), one value missing; write it in the slot

mixed_frac_qs.name: Mixed Fraction Questions
mixed_frac_qs.teaches: choosing the operation (+, −, x, ÷ by an integer) for fraction problems in context: perimeter, area, sharing, totals
mixed_frac_qs.representation: a mixed page: one boxed word-work cell per item, the story in Andika with a bar or shape drawing, an operation box the pupil fills with +, −, x or ÷, then the calculation with fraction slots; the operation box is empty from the first page (only the model page shows it filled) and the drawing fades on later pages
mixed_frac_qs.why: mixed_fraction_ops is a random pool (also missing numerators, bare calculations and whole ÷ unit fraction items); no page asks the pupil to choose among +, −, x and ÷ by an integer in context.

mult_mixed_int.name: Multiply a Mixed Number by an Integer (option)
mult_mixed_int.teaches: multiplying a mixed number by a whole number (2 1/3 × 4)
mult_mixed_int.representation: a mixed-number band on mult_frac_whole: one boxed cell, 2 1/3 x 4 in Andika with a fraction slot (whole, numerator, denominator boxes); hint row shows 4 bars of 2 1/3, fades
mult_mixed_int.why: mult_frac_whole deals proper fractions only; Y6 also multiplies mixed numbers by integers.

mult_three.name: Multiply Three Numbers
mult_three.teaches: multiplying three 1-digit numbers using the associative property (2 × 5 × 7 = 10 × 7)
mult_three.representation: three-factor expressions with a bracket prompt to choose the easy pair first
mult_three.why: Y4 Multiply three numbers (prior learning wk W11 and W33) has no skill.

multi_step_four_ops.option: two steps with × and ÷ (3 packs of 6, 4 eaten), write the equation with a letter for the unknown, remainder steps, and a "reasonable?" estimate
multi_step_four_ops.name: Two-Step Problems With All Four Operations (option)
multi_step_four_ops.teaches: two-step and multistep word problems with the four operations, represented by an equation with a letter, remainders interpreted, and checked by estimating
multi_step_four_ops.representation: word-work cell: the story in Andika, a two-part bar model frame (structural), a working box, step-answer slots then the final answer slot with a unit label
multi_step_four_ops.why: multi_step_word is + and - within 100 only; Y6 multi-step problems mix all four operations with large numbers.

negative_count.name: Count Through Zero
negative_count.teaches: negative numbers in context (temperature), counting through zero in 1s and multiples, and the difference between a positive and a negative number
negative_count.representation: one boxed cell: a vertical B&W thermometer scale (-10 to 10, every unit ticked, every 2 labelled) with two temperatures marked; write the difference in degrees in the slot
negative_count.why: Y6 negative numbers finds intervals across zero in context (temperature); no skill asks the difference across 0.

net_draw.name: Complete the Net (option)
net_draw.teaches: deciding whether a net folds into a cube or cuboid, and completing a net by adding the missing face
net_draw.representation: a net on squared paper with one face missing; shade where the face goes, or tick Yes / No for "folds into a cube"
net_draw.why: net_identify only matches a net to its solid (multiple choice); WRM also draws and checks nets.

nl_20.name: Numbers on a Number Line (any scale)
nl_20.teaches: the number line as a counting and place-value tool: count along, find, place and estimate numbers on 0-20, 0-50, 0-100, 0-1,000, 0-10,000 and 0-1,000,000 lines, counting in 1s, 10s, 100s ... and with only some ticks labelled; Y6 extends the ladder to 0-10,000,000 lines (ends consecutive hundred-thousands or millions)
nl_20.representation: a drawn number line with some ticks labelled; write the number at the arrow, or mark a number; option: scale; option: estimate on a line with only the ends marked. Y6 cell: one boxed cell, a black line with both end values printed and 10 interval ticks, an arrow to read (write the number in the slot) or a 7-digit number to mark
nl_20.why: Existing number-line proposal reaches 0-1,000,000 (Y5.B1.S9); extend its scale ladder to 0-10,000,000 for Y6 rather than add a second number-line skill.

pairs_values.name: Pairs of Values and Two Unknowns
pairs_values.teaches: finding all whole-number pairs that satisfy an equation (a + b = 8, 2a + b = 10) and solving simple problems with two unknowns
pairs_values.representation: one boxed cell: a two-column a | b table with 5 empty rows for a + b = 10 (or 3a = b); list the pairs systematically; option: a bar model problem with two unknowns
pairs_values.why: no skill lists solution pairs of a two-letter equation or solves two-unknown problems

parallelogram.name: Area of a Parallelogram
parallelogram.teaches: area of a parallelogram as base × perpendicular height, by cutting and moving a triangle
parallelogram.representation: a parallelogram on squared paper with the height dashed; write the area
parallelogram.why: No live skill deals the area of a parallelogram.

pct_one_step.option: set "Percents" with values 50, 25, 10, 1 (and 20, 5); default 50, 25, 10, 1 for this step
pct_one_step.name: Percentage of an Amount: One Step (option)
pct_one_step.teaches: finding 50%, 25%, 10% and 1% of an amount by one division (halve, quarter, ÷ 10, ÷ 100), one percent per page first
pct_one_step.representation: one boxed cell: a B&W bar with the amount on the whole brace and "100%" under it, split into 2, 4, 10 or 100 equal parts (the split is the fading hint; the bar frame is structural); "10% of 60 = [ ]" with the answer slot; no division sign is printed, the pupil chooses it
pct_one_step.why: percent_of_number has no option to choose the percents and mixes multi-step percents (and wrong 33% items) into every page

percent_multi.name: Percentages: Multi-Step and Missing Values (option)
percent_multi.teaches: percentage of an amount in two steps (increase/decrease), and missing values (what percent is 12 of 40?)
percent_multi.representation: word-work cell: a two-step percentage story (find 30%, then the amount left) with a 100% bar model frame (structural) and two answer slots; missing-percentage cell: "12 out of 40 = [ ] %" with a bar of 40 on the whole brace and "100%" under it, 12 shaded; the pupil writes the percent
percent_multi.why: no skill builds a percent from 10%/5%/1%, does increase/decrease, or finds the missing percentage

pie.name: Pie Charts
pie.teaches: reading pie charts with fractions and percentages and drawing them from angles (360°)
pie.representation: one boxed cell: a B&W circle split into sectors (black radii, sector labels by fraction or percent); write the amount for one sector given the total; option: draw from a table with a printed 10-degree ring
pie.why: pie_chart only reads a printed percent; reading fractions of a whole, amounts from a total, and drawing from angles are missing.

protractor_read.name: Measure With a Protractor (option)
protractor_read.teaches: measuring angles in whole degrees with a protractor: which scale, from 0
protractor_read.option: form "read the protractor": a protractor drawn over the angle; write the degrees (not multiple choice)
protractor_read.representation: one boxed cell: a printed B&W protractor over an angle, both scales labelled every 10 degrees; write the angle in the slot; the inner/outer scale cue fades
protractor_read.why: measure_angles is multiple choice over multiples of 30/45; WRM measures any angle to the nearest degree with a protractor.

pv10_exponents.option: notation "powers written with exponents" (× 10³) and task "compare powers of ten by counting zeros"
pv10_exponents.name: Powers of Ten With Exponents (option)
pv10_exponents.teaches: the pattern of zeros and of the decimal point when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10, written with whole-number exponents
pv10_exponents.representation: one boxed cell: 10,000 = 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 = 10^□ with a small write-in slot for the exponent (or the number); powers-of-10 chart as a fading hint row

pv10x_dp.name: Multiply and Divide Decimals by 10, 100, 1,000: Up to 3 Decimal Places (option)
pv10x_dp.teaches: multiplying and dividing numbers with 1, 2 or 3 decimal places (and decimals below 1) by 10, 100 and 1,000, writing placeholder zeros (0.307 x 1,000 = 307; 3.4 ÷ 100 = 0.034)
pv10x_dp.representation: the existing pv shift-chart cell (Th H T O . t h th, black lines, the digits drawn in the start row and empty boxes in the answer row); the arrows showing the shift are the fading hint; write the answer in the slot
pv10x_dp.why: the Decimals option deals only 1-dp numbers × a power and whole numbers ÷ a power

ratio_fraction.name: Ratio and Fractions (option)
ratio_fraction.teaches: linking ratio and fractions (3 : 2 means 3/5 of the whole) with a bar model
ratio_fraction.representation: one boxed cell: a bar model of two colours (black and hatched parts) labelled in the ratio; write the fraction of the whole for one colour in a fraction slot
ratio_fraction.why: ratio_intro never turns a ratio into fractions of the whole

ratio_language.name: Ratio Language (option)
ratio_language.teaches: describing a ratio in words from a picture: "for every 2 red counters there are 3 blue counters", including the reverse sentence
ratio_language.representation: a boxed cell with a row of line-drawn counters (filled and open circles, no colour) and the sentence frame "For every [ ] ___ there are [ ] ___"; word bank for the object names; numbers only to write
ratio_language.why: WRM teaches ratio language before the colon; ratio_intro starts at the colon
ratio_language.option: variant "for every … there are …" from a picture (no colon)

ratio_problems.name: Ratio and Proportion Problems
ratio_problems.teaches: ratio, proportion and recipe problems solved with a bar model or ratio table
ratio_problems.representation: word-work cell: a short ratio story, a bar model or 2-row ratio table frame (structural), and one answer slot with a unit label
ratio_problems.why: sharing in a ratio, two-step proportion stories and recipes are dealt by no skill

reflect_grid.name: Reflect on a Grid
reflect_grid.teaches: reflecting a shape in a horizontal or vertical mirror line on a square grid (Y5), then in the x- and y-axes in all four quadrants, writing the new coordinates (Y6)
reflect_grid.representation: one boxed cell: the B&W coord-grid (four quadrants to ±6, black axes, grey grid) with a dashed mirror line (an axis) and a shape in black; draw the reflection, or write the image coordinates "( [ ], [ ] )" in slots; the key shows the image
reflect_grid.why: geo_reflect is multiple choice over the axes; Y6 draws the reflection and writes the new coordinates.

reflex_angles.name: Reflex Angles (option)
reflex_angles.teaches: naming reflex angles (more than 180 degrees) alongside acute, right, obtuse and straight
reflex_angles.representation: one boxed cell: an angle drawn with the arc on the outside; tick the name (acute / obtuse / reflex) from a word bank, then write its size as 360 minus the inner angle
reflex_angles.why: identify_angles offers right, acute, obtuse and straight but not reflex, which Y6 classifies.

round_whole.name: Round Decimals to the Nearest Whole (option)
round_whole.teaches: rounding a 1-dp or 2-dp decimal to the nearest whole number on a number line
round_whole.representation: one boxed cell: a decimal on a number line between two wholes (both ends labelled, tenths ticked); write the nearest whole number in the slot; the line fades
round_whole.why: no skill rounds a decimal to the nearest whole number

same_area.name: Same Area, Different Perimeter
same_area.teaches: shapes with the same area but different perimeters, and the reverse
same_area.representation: one boxed cell with two or three rectangles drawn on a 1 cm square grid (black outlines, grey grid); write area and perimeter in a small table under each; tick the pair with the same area (or the same perimeter)
same_area.why: No skill compares several shapes with equal area and different perimeters (or the reverse); area_perimeter does one rectangle at a time.

scale.name: Scale Drawing and Scale Factors
scale.teaches: enlarging shapes by a scale factor, scale drawings and similar shapes (find the missing side)
scale.representation: shapes on squared paper with one side of the image given; write the scale factor or the missing side
scale.why: no skill enlarges a shape, reads a scale drawing or compares similar shapes

square_cube.name: Square and Cube Numbers
square_cube.teaches: square numbers as square arrays and cube numbers as cubes, with the notation 5² and 2³
square_cube.representation: one boxed cell: a square dot array or a drawn cube of cubes; write the number and its notation (4² = 16) in two slots; option: tick "is it a square number?"
square_cube.why: exponents_simple evaluates 5² but never shows squares as arrays or cubes as cubes, nor asks "is it a square number?".

thousandths_pv.name: Thousandths (option)
thousandths_pv.teaches: thousandths as fractions and decimals and on a place-value chart
thousandths_pv.representation: one boxed cell: a place-value chart to thousandths (O . Tth Hth Thth) with digits; write the number or the value of a digit in the slot
thousandths_pv.why: Y5.B7.S7 Thousandths on a place value chart (prior learning) has no skill

translate_grid.name: Translate on a Grid
translate_grid.teaches: translating a point or shape and describing a translation (3 right, 2 up): first quadrant (Y4/Y5), then in all four quadrants with the new coordinates written (Y6)
translate_grid.representation: one boxed cell: the B&W coord-grid (black axes, grey grid, first quadrant to 10 or four quadrants to ±6), the shape drawn in black; draw the image, or write the move "[ ] right/left, [ ] up/down" (word banks, no direction given) or the new coordinates "( [ ], [ ] )" in slots
translate_grid.why: geo_translate is multiple choice (pick the image); Y6 draws the image in four quadrants, describes the move and writes the new coordinates.

value_ten_times.option: form "ten times / one tenth": compare the value of the same digit in two places (the 7 in 700 is 10 times the 7 in 70; 700 ÷ 70 = 10)
value_ten_times.name: Ten Times the Place to the Right (option)
value_ten_times.teaches: a digit in one place is worth 10 times what it is worth in the place to its right and 1/10 of the place to its left
value_ten_times.representation: one boxed cell: two place-value charts stacked, the same digit circled in each; sentence frame "The 7 in 700 is ___ times the 7 in 70" with one write-in slot (10, 100 or 1/10)
value_ten_times.why: Y6 Powers of 10 is the x10 relationship between neighbouring places, which no skill asks directly.

vis_bar_family.option: model: 'bar' on algebra:write_equation (part-whole bar with letters) and on conversions:percent_visual (the percentage bar)
vis_bar_family.name: The Bar-Model Family (every WRM bar)
vis_bar_family.teaches: the WRM bar models as kit cells: a part-whole bar with letters to form an equation from (n and 5 make 12 -> n + 5 = 12), and the percentage bar ("100%" over 2-20 equal cells) to read percentages of a whole not split into 100
vis_bar_family.representation: one boxed cell: a B&W bar (black outline, equal or labelled parts, the single grey for shaded parts) with a brace for the whole; equation form: letter n in one part, 5 in the other, 12 on the brace, write the equation on the answer line with no operation sign printed; percentage form: "100%" on the brace, 4, 5, 10 or 20 cells, some shaded, write the percent shaded in the slot
vis_bar_family.why: Existing visual build (the bar-model family); no live skill forms an equation from a bar or reads a percent of a whole split into fewer than 100 parts.

vis_division_layouts.name: Division Layouts: Bus Stop, Notes, Missing Digits
vis_division_layouts.representation: the division template gains `layout: 'short'` (bus stop with small exchange-digit slots, an r slot, a decimal point and trailing zeros), `support: 'multiples'` (a multiples list beside), step notes, and `unknown` digits; box_division_* leave the legacy path
vis_division_layouts.teaches: the division template gains `layout: 'short'` (bus stop with small exchange-digit slots, an r slot, a decimal point and trailing zeros), `support: 'multiples'` (a multiples list beside), step notes, and `unknown` digits; box_division_* leave the legacy path
vis_division_layouts.option: Division Layouts: Bus Stop, Notes, Missing Digits
vis_division_layouts.why: The division template has no bus-stop (short division) layout with exchange-digit slots.

vis_hundred_square.name: Hundred Square as One Whole (and the thousand square)
vis_hundred_square.teaches: percent as parts of 100 on a B&W hundred square, including the part not shaded (complement to 100%) and shading a given percent
vis_hundred_square.representation: one boxed cell: a 10 x 10 square, black outline and grey grid, part shaded with the single grey; two slots "shaded [ ] %" and "not shaded [ ] %"; for "shade" the grid is blank and the pupil shades it
vis_hundred_square.why: Existing visual build: its complement mode closes "the part not shaded", and a blank grid stops the shade item giving its answer away.

vis_mean_levelling.name: The Mean as Levelling
vis_mean_levelling.representation: `support: 'level'` on the mean: objects per person → pooled → equal rows; towers levelled
vis_mean_levelling.why: The WRM lesson introduces the mean as levelling towers; the visual option is already listed.
vis_mean_levelling.teaches: the mean as levelling: pool the objects and share them into equal rows or towers

vis_pv_bands_millions.name: Widen Place Value to 7 Digits (millions)
vis_pv_bands_millions.representation: bands 99,999 / 999,999 / 9,999,999 on place_value_disks, pv_disks_build, compare, expand, value and number_word_names; period heads (Millions | Thousands | Ones, H T O under each, commas in threes); million bands on rounding_visual / round_nl_*; the odometer digit display. pv_digit_drag's band is `big_numbers`
vis_pv_bands_millions.teaches: bands 99,999 / 999,999 / 9,999,999 on place_value_disks, pv_disks_build, compare, expand, value and number_word_names; period heads (Millions | Thousands | Ones, H T O under each, commas in threes); million bands on rounding_visual / round_nl_*; the odometer digit display. pv_digit_drag's band is `big_numbers`
vis_pv_bands_millions.why: The place-value chart needs a Millions period (M | HTh TTh Th | H T O) to show 7-digit numbers.

vis_value_line_vertical.name: Vertical Number Line Through Zero
vis_value_line_vertical.representation: value-line gains `orientation: 'vertical'` (a lift panel, a sea-level scale) and a thermometer look (`line: 'thermometer'`) through zero
vis_value_line_vertical.teaches: value-line gains `orientation: 'vertical'` (a lift panel, a sea-level scale) and a thermometer look (`line: 'thermometer'`) through zero
vis_value_line_vertical.why: A vertical thermometer line through zero is the WRM picture for temperature intervals.

volume_cubes.name: Volume by Counting Cubes
volume_cubes.teaches: volume as the number of unit cubes (cm³), comparing volumes and estimating volume and capacity
volume_cubes.representation: isometric drawings of cube solids; write how many cubes / cm³; option: which has more
volume_cubes.why: No live skill counts unit cubes in a drawn solid; volume starts at l x w x h.

wp_long_div.option: multi-digit numbers: up to 4-digit / 2-digit, remainder interpreted
wp_long_div.name: Long Division Word Problems (option)
wp_long_div.teaches: division stories that need short or long division of 3-4 digit numbers by 1- or 2-digit divisors, with the remainder interpreted (round up, round down, or as a fraction)
wp_long_div.representation: word-work cell: the story in Andika, a bar model frame below (structural, stays), a working box with the long-division bracket grid, one answer slot with a unit label and a tick box: round up / round down / remainder
wp_long_div.why: div_word_problems and remainder_interpret use divisor <= 20 and dividend <= 10 x divisor; Y6 problems need long division.

wp_multidigit.name: Multi-Digit Word Problems (option)
wp_multidigit.teaches: one- and two-step multiplication stories that need a written method (1,250 seats x 24 rows)
wp_multidigit.representation: word-work cell: the story in Andika, a bar model frame below (structural, stays), a working box with the column multiplication grid, one answer slot with a unit label; no pictures in the plain variant
wp_multidigit.why: Every multiplication word problem uses fact-sized numbers; Y6 stories need long multiplication.
